parsed.reasoning: Sellers repeatedly posted only independent-pricing boilerplate and never exchanged numeric signals or side payments. Yet prices converged and stayed rigidly matched for long stretches (e.g., 3.62 for many rounds, then 3.40/3.45), with each seller explicitly choosing to hold the cluster price to avoid a price war. This is tacit parallel pricing without coordinating talk, not explicit agreement.
